items.q: Match the following drug class to its mechanism — 1) Biguanide 2) Sulfonylurea 3) SGLT2 inhibitor 4) DPP-4 inhibitor … A) Activates AMPK; reduces hepatic gluconeogenesis B) Closes β-cell K-ATP channels C) Blocks renal glucose reabsorption D) Prevents GLP-1 breakdown
items.exp: Metformin activates AMPK and reduces hepatic gluconeogenesis; sulfonylureas close K-ATP channels; SGLT2 inhibitors block renal glucose reabsorption; DPP-4 inhibitors prolong GLP-1 action. (Book p933)

items.q: A patient with T2DM and HFREF (HFrEF) needs an antihyperglycaemic agent with proven mortality benefit. The most appropriate class is:
items.exp: SGLT2 inhibitors (empagliflozin, dapagliflozin) reduce HF hospitalisation and CV mortality in HFrEF regardless of diabetes status. (Book p933)

items.q: Assess drug classes: I Metformin activates AMPK. II Gliclazide is the only sulfonylurea with reported cardio-renal benefit.
items.exp: Metformin activates AMPK; gliclazide is highlighted as the sulfonylurea with the best cardiovascular safety profile. (Book p933)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a class that does not have established cardiovascular outcome benefit?
items.exp: Sulfonylureas have neutral or adverse cardiovascular outcome data (except gliclazide); SGLT2i and GLP-1 agonists reduce MACE; pioglitazone is contraindicated in HF. (Book p933)

items.q: SGLT2 inhibitors block the ___ cotransporter in the proximal convoluted tubule.
items.exp: SGLT2 inhibitors block sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 in the PCT, producing glycosuria. (Book p933)

items.q: Match the following agent to a special indication on the page — 1) Empagliflozin 2) Liraglutide 3) Linagliptin 4) Saroglitazar … A) HFrEF mortality benefit B) Cardiovascular outcome benefit (LEADER) C) Renal-safe DPP-4 inhibitor D) NASH / dyslipidaemia dual PPAR agonist
items.exp: Empagliflozin has HFrEF mortality benefit; liraglutide has CV outcome benefit (LEADER); linagliptin is renal-safe without dose adjustment; saroglitazar is a dual PPAR agonist for NASH/dyslipidaemia. (Book p933)

items.q: A patient with T2DM and CKD stage 3 needs intensification with minimal renal dose adjustment. The most appropriate add-on is:
items.exp: Linagliptin is excreted via bile and needs no renal dose adjustment; sitagliptin needs dose reduction; pioglitazone carries fluid-retention risk in CKD. (Book p933)

items.q: Assess GLP-1 RAs: I Oral semaglutide is available. II Semaglutide is contraindicated in pregnancy.
items.exp: Oral semaglutide is approved; GLP-1 RAs are not approved in pregnancy and should be stopped before conception. (Book p933)

items.q: Match the following drug to its side-effect profile — 1) Pioglitazone 2) SGLT2 inhibitor 3) GLP-1 RA 4) DPP-4 inhibitor … A) Fluid retention and fracture risk B) Genital mycotic infection C) Nausea and pancreatitis D) Nasopharyngitis, rare pancreatitis
items.exp: Pioglitazone causes fluid retention, fracture and bladder cancer risk; SGLT2i cause genital mycotic infection; GLP-1 RA cause nausea and pancreatitis risk; DPP-4 inhibitors cause nasopharyngitis and rare pancreatitis. (Book p933)

items.q: A T2DM patient on metformin develops recurrent genital thrush and is started on empagliflozin. The most appropriate counselling is:
opts: Maintain perineal hygiene and report genital infections early
items.exp: SGLT2 inhibitors increase genital mycotic infection risk; maintain hygiene and seek review if symptoms develop. (Book p933)

items.q: Pioglitazone acts as a ___ receptor agonist, increasing insulin sensitivity in adipose tissue.
items.exp: Pioglitazone is a PPARγ agonist, increasing adipose insulin sensitivity. (Book p933)

items.q: Assess TZDs: I Pioglitazone is contraindicated in heart failure. II Rosiglitazone has been withdrawn from most markets due to CV concerns.
items.exp: Pioglitazone is contraindicated in HF (fluid retention); rosiglitazone use is heavily restricted due to CV concerns. (Book p933)
